title: NEB Class 11 Mathematics — Calculus — 2021
subject: mathematics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Using the first principles of differentiation, show that $\displaystyle \frac{d}{dx}\left(x^{1/3}\right)=\frac{1}{3x^{2/3}}$. Hence find the derivative of $y=(2x+3)^{1/3}$.
questions.solution:
Let $y=x^{1/3}$. Then
$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{(x+h)^{1/3}-x^{1/3}}{h}$$
Put $a=x^{1/3}$ and $b=(x+h)^{1/3}$. Then
$$b^{3}-a^{3}=h\;\Longrightarrow\;(b-a)(b^{2}+ab+a^{2})=h\;\Longrightarrow\;b-a=\frac{h}{b^{2}+ab+a^{2}}$$
$$\therefore\ \frac{dy}{dx}=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{1}{b^{2}+ab+a^{2}}=\frac{1}{3a^{2}}=\frac{1}{3x^{2/3}}$$

**Hence**, for $y=(2x+3)^{1/3}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{3}(2x+3)^{-2/3}\times 2=\boxed{\frac{2}{3(2x+3)^{2/3}}}$$
questions.knowledgeNote: First principles uses $a^{3}-b^{3}=(a-b)(a^{2}+ab+b^{2})$; the increment $h$ cancels and the result follows by substitution.
